candidates.title: How Micron Became A $1.3 Trillion AI Winner
candidates.description: First, Apple is rolling out the biggest hardware price increase in its history — MacBooks up as much as $300, iPads up $200, with the Vision Pro, Apple TV, and HomePod all climbing 15 to 25%. The reason isn't tariffs or a new chip. It's memory. AI data centers have triggered a DRAM shortage so severe that prices spiked as much as 98% in a single quarter, an event the industry is calling "RAMageddon." We explain why Micron, the company that makes those chips, has seen its stock rocket while Apple's slid 6% on the same news — and why your back-to-school laptop just became the most expensive in decades. Then, Hill House Home built a $110 million business off essentially one product: the Nap Dre

candidates.title: Netflix Just Turned Your Phone Into A Nintendo
candidates.description: Netflix is turning your phone into a video game controller. On June 30 it launches Unhinged, an interactive horror game starring Zoe Kravitz and Sadie Sink, where you scan a QR code and your real phone becomes the flashlight your character uses to survive the dark. When a killer calls from inside the game, your actual phone rings. Netflix has quietly had games since 2021 with almost nothing to show for it, so why is it now spending Hollywood money to build a console-free game for people who don't even play games? candidates.title: Meta's New Glasses Could Make Zuckerberg A Trillionaire
candidates.description: Meta just dropped Ray-Ban from its smart glasses entirely. After selling at least 9 million Ray-Ban Meta pairs, Zuckerberg unveiled a trio of his own AI frames — the Fury, the Adventurer, and a Kylie Jenner-designed edition — starting at $299, about $80 cheaper than last year's Ray-Ban model and roughly 90% less than Snap's $2,000 face computer. But the real story isn't the price. Meta is treating smart glasses like a car company, with a model for every tier, plans to strip out the cameras for a sub-$100 audio pair, and even facial recognition that tells you who you're looking at. We break down why these frames are really Zuckerberg's bid to replace the iPhone — and become the world's second

candidates.title: Google's $75M A24 Deal Could Reshape Every Movie
candidates.description: Google just took a $75 million equity stake in A24 — its first-ever investment in a film studio — and tied it to a multi-year AI research partnership with DeepMind. While most of Hollywood is busy suing AI companies for copyright infringement, the anti-blockbuster studio behind Everything Everywhere All at Once is doing the exact opposite. The DeepMind tools are aimed at reshoots, editing, and VFX rather than generating films outright. We get into why Google is double-dipping on the future of Hollywood — it already owns YouTube — and whether this deal is a genuine creative breakthrough or something we're calling "taste-washing." Then, Grillo's Pickles added 100,000 followers in a single week

candidates.title: One Rule Beats Every Amazon Prime Day Deal
candidates.description: A new lawsuit claims Amazon's Prime Day is "rife with fake sales" — and this year the event runs a full four days. We dug into the pricing playbook nearly every major retailer leans on, from phantom "regular" prices that were never real to the countdown timers engineered to make you skip the math. Then we lay out how to call the bluff: the free price-history tool that exposes a fake discount in seconds, the chatbot trick that quietly talks the price down, and why this could be the last Prime Day your emotions can be used against you. candidates.title: Ben & Jerry's Founder On Being Silenced
candidates.description: We sit down with Ben Cohen, the co-founder of Ben & Jerry's, who is now fighting to buy back the company that still carries his name. Back in 2000, he and Jerry Greenfield sold Ben & Jerry's to Unilever for $326 million — but structured one of the most unusual deals in corporate history to protect the brand's social mission. Now Ben says the corporate owners have muzzled the brand he built, his best friend and co-founder Jerry has resigned, and Ben has launched a campaign to free Ben & Jerry's. We ask him whether mixing politics and business is actually profitable, what Ben & Jerry's 2.0 would look like, and how far he'll go to win it back. candidates.title: How SpaceX Turned Into Elon's $2T ATM
candidates.description: SpaceX IPO'd on Friday, and within one trading day it became the first mega meme stock in history. Elon Musk sold $86 billion in shares — 90% of it to Wall Street — and then retail investors did something almost no one predicted: by Monday, 74% of every single-stock purchase they made was SpaceX, sending the stock up 50%. Here's the twist. With shares soaring and only 4% of the company actually available to trade, Musk immediately started selling. We break down what he did with the money in just three business days, and the one advantage he has that no other CEO on earth can copy.
